leading_positions.synthesis: Four members include base editing as a prize part, and all four now name David R. Liu alone (Chabes and Aili moved from Komor and Gaudelli in response to the chair). They differ on its partner: Aili pairs it with B016, Chabes and Linke with B018, Somfai with B002. They also differ on how much weight base editing can carry alone, since Aili and Somfai say a base-editing-led prize would read as a second genome-editing award after 2020 and want a mature partner. Nishida and Kondo (Target-AID) are acknowledged by several members as a parallel claim that is not resolved by the Liu-only wording.

Four members include targeted protein degradation as a prize part and agree that induced proximity is a new pharmacological principle. They split on laureates: Aqvist and Sparr name Crews, Deshaies and Handa to span the PROTAC and cereblon-glue strands, while Chabes and Linke name Crews and Deshaies only and treat the glue branch as a separate achievement. Aqvist and Sparr both flag Ciulli's VHL ligand work as the weakest exclusion. Every supporter concedes that no degrader drug is approved. Aqvist and Sparr hold B018 as the whole prize, whereas Chabes and Linke pair it with B029.

Chabes and Linke share the same two-part configuration, Liu for base editing and Crews with Deshaies for PROTACs. Both parts are chemical biology with unapproved or early clinical outcomes, which both name as the main risk. Their citations differ in wording but not in laureates. No other member lists this exact pairing.

Somfai and Zou both name Buchwald and Hartwig for Pd-catalysed C-N coupling, and others (Aili, Linke) acknowledge its clean attribution and maturity. They differ on structure: Zou proposes it alone, while Somfai pairs it with B029 (Liu). Both deal with the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the Kosugi precedent in the same way, as a matter for the citation or background text and not for the laureate list.

Aili alone proposes ionizable lipid nanoparticles (Cullis and Hope) with base editing (Liu), presenting both as chemical enabling layers under nucleic-acid medicine. No other member prefers B016, though Aqvist, Linke, Somfai and Sparr list it as an alternative, and the open points are the diffuse credit (Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson, Langer) and overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize.

Brzezinski alone prefers nitrogenase (Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt) with a citation built on structure of the FeMo-cofactor and not on a closed mechanism. Zou regards the structural evidence as first rank and lists B006 as an alternative, but others say the N2 binding site and catalytic intermediates are not settled.

areas_of_agreement: No member prefers a single configuration shared by a majority of five; the eight files give four explicit supporters each for B029 and B018, two for B002, and one each for B016 and B006.
Members who include base editing converge on a Liu-only laureate list as the cleanest attribution, while still noting Nishida and Kondo as a parallel line.
Members describe induced proximity as a genuinely new concept, including those who rank B018 as an alternative and not as their first choice.
Members regard B002 as having the cleanest attribution and the strongest maturity record, whatever they think of its novelty after 2010.
Every member who includes B018 states that no approved degrader drug is confirmed.

Several members say B052 phase separation, with unsettled physiological relevance, is not mature enough for this year's prize; Sparr, who placed it first in her opening, has moved away from it for that reason.
All eight members report no specific conflict or recusal need.
scientific_disputes: Whether base editing adds chemistry beyond the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize: Aili and Chabes see a defined deamination reaction directed to one nucleotide in a living cell, while Somfai and Sparr describe it as evolved-enzyme chemistry and an engineering fusion on the recognised nickase platform.

Whether PROTAC design is new chemistry or medicinal-chemistry optimisation of ligand-linker-ligand compounds (Somfai's concern), against Aqvist's view that ternary-complex cooperativity, E3 hijack and the cereblon mechanism are the new chemical content.

Whether C-N coupling is a distinct achievement from the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize: Zou points to its own ligand design and amine-binding mechanism, while Somfai and Linke ask what new principle goes beyond ligand optimisation and the shared Pd(0)/Pd(II) manifold.
Whether a nitrogenase citation can be framed around structure while N2 binding and the intermediates remain open (Brzezinski for, Chabes and Zou cautious).

Whether the ionizable lipid design principle (pKa tuning, self-assembly, fusogenic phase behaviour) is chemistry or engineering, and whether it is separable from the 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside modification.
attribution_disputes: B029: Liu alone is the common formulation, but Komor and Gaudelli (lead first authors) and Nishida and Kondo (Target-AID) have claims that the files either set aside or raise as unresolved.

B018: whether PROTAC (Crews, Deshaies, with Ciulli and Sakamoto as possible additions) and cereblon glue (Handa, Ito) are one achievement or two. Aqvist and Sparr name Crews, Deshaies and Handa. Chabes and Linke name Crews and Deshaies. Aqvist is open to swapping Handa for Ciulli, and Brzezinski says a combined prize forces an arbitrary split.
B016: no common trio exists; Aili names Cullis and Hope, and several members say Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer each have a plausible claim.
B002: Buchwald and Hartwig are uncontested as a pair, but the Kosugi tin-amide precedent has to be placed in the citation or in background text.
B006: five-person credit (Dean, Ribbe, Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt) is cut to Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt, which omits Dean and Ribbe.
B069: Brzezinski and Aili both say credit among Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer, Bayley and Akeson is hard to separate, while Linke's file ranks it as an alternative.
maturity_disputes: B018: no approved degrader is confirmed in any file; members differ on whether independent confirmation and the clinical pipeline are enough, or whether B016 or B002 should come first.

B029: base-editing clinical outcomes are early and the 2020 CRISPR prize is recent; Somfai and Aili say this argues for a mature partner, while Chabes and Linke accept it as the cost of a two-part prize.
B002 is mature but, by Somfai's own account, may be overdue and is also an extension of an area honoured in 2010; there is no disagreement about its timing, only about its novelty.
B006: whether a structure-based citation is mature while the mechanism is still debated, and whether the recent cryo-EM turnover states need independent reproduction (Chabes).
B052: whether in vivo relevance and the definition of phase separation will be settled soon enough for a prize in the next few years.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: No member discloses a specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate. Disclosed general ties: Lund affiliation shared by Linke, Somfai and Sparr, and the Stockholm University colleagueship of Brzezinski and Zou, none of which involves a credited name.
Chabes says he would recuse if any candidate turned out to be a collaborator from the Umea, Rothstein or Stillman networks.
Sparr notes that her lipid self-assembly work is close to B016 and B052 but states no personal or institutional tie to any credited name.
questions_for_round2: Is a Liu-only citation for B029 defensible given the Nishida and Kondo Target-AID priority claim, and should the wording be limited to the engineered base-editor concept with prime editing (B028) kept outside it?

For B018, should the citation cover only PROTACs and induced proximity (Crews and Deshaies, with Ciulli as a possible third name), or also the cereblon and molecular-glue strand (Handa), and if the glue branch is wanted should it be argued as its own part?

Can members who rank B018 above B016 or B002 justify a prize before any degrader drug is approved, and is there a stated evidence threshold, such as a regulatory approval, that would change anyone's ranking?
Can Somfai and Zou state in one sentence the new chemical principle in B002 that goes beyond the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize, and would Linke or Aili then move B002 into their configuration?

Between a two-part prize of B029 with B018, B002 or B016 and a single-achievement prize, which structure can the committee explain to a broad audience, given that B029 or B018 each has only four explicit supporters?
Can anyone propose a defensible three-name subset for B016, given the Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer claims and the 2023 Medicine overlap, or should it be dropped from consideration?
Should the committee set aside B006 and B052 for this cycle on maturity, or does Brzezinski's structure-only framing of nitrogenase warrant a full comparison in round 2?
summary.chair_observation: The eight round-1 files show convergence on a small set of topics but not on a configuration: B029 and B018 each have four explicit supporters, B002 two, and B016 and B006 one each. The chief unresolved points are the novelty of base editing and PROTACs relative to the 2020 CRISPR and 2010 cross-coupling prizes, the clinical maturity of both, and whether the PROTAC and glue strands are one or two achievements. The chair is himself a supporter of the B029 with B018 configuration, and this summary counts only what the files state.
